questions.q: 'Look! The baby ___(cry).' Which form and why?
questions.a: 'is crying' — 'look!' signals happening-now → continuous. A wrong answer 'cries' reveals the student ignores signal words; 'is cry'/'crying' alone shows the missing-helper error.

questions.q: Fix: 'I am going to school every day.'
questions.a: 'I go to school every day' — 'every day' is a habit → simple present. A wrong answer keeping 'am going' shows the student defaults to continuous whenever the action feels current.
swimming (double m after short vowel), dancing (drop silent e), sitting (double t). Wrong answers 'swiming/danceing' show the two spelling rules aren't yet automatic.

questions.q: Present tense has two gears students must separate: simple present for habits and facts ('She reads daily', 'The sun rises in the east') versus present ______ for actions happening NOW ('She is reading').

Fill in the blank: Present tense has two gears students must separate: simple present for habits and facts ('She reads daily', 'The sun rises in the east') versus present ______ for actions happening NOW ('She is reading').
Fill in the blank: Two pictures: a girl who reads every day vs a girl reading right now. 'She reads daily' — habit, simple. 'She is reading' — now, ______.
Fill in the blank: Mixing them is the most common class-______ tense error.
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student chooses simple present vs present continuous by asking 'habit/fact or happening-now?', uses is/am/are + V-ing correctly, and handles the spelling rules (run→running, write→writing).
